newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans listening to more radio in 1997 - report.
newsitem.headline: Germans listening to more radio in 1997 - report.

text.p: The German radio market has expanded again this year, with now over 80 percent of adults listening to the medium every day, the German unit of media marketing company IP said on Wednesday.
Based on the results of its annual Media Analysis, IP said 82.5 percent of Germans over the age of 14 turn on a radio daily, up from 79.8 percent in 1996.
The company also said Germans have been listening to their radios for longer periods of time in 1997, an average of 177 minutes daily, eight minutes more than in the previous year.
IP said both private and public stations had benefited from the medium's growth. The ARD public network has posted gains of 2.6 percent this year and private stations have seen a 8.2 percent boost.

"This development again highlights that target-group and regional-focus formatting in the German radio market is succeeding," IP said in a statement. "That is especially true for the most competitive market, Berlin-Brandenburg."
The company said the Berlin and neighbouring Brandenburg market had grown in 1997 to 84.9 percent of adults listening daily, up from 83.8 percent in the previous year.
